title: Indian-origin investors now run some of Silicon Valley's biggest venture funds - and the money is flowing back
sources: TiE (The Indus Entrepreneurs), 2025 - global chapter and mentor network data
Inc42 / Tracxn, 2025 - Indian-origin venture partners at major US VC firms
NASSCOM, 2025 - diaspora angel investment into Indian startups
caption:
Some of the biggest checks written into Indian startups don't come from India. They come from Indian-origin investors sitting inside Silicon Valley's top venture firms.

TiE, The Indus Entrepreneurs, now runs more than 60 chapters worldwide, built almost entirely by Indian-origin founders and investors. Partners of Indian origin now sit inside firms like Sequoia, Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst as decision-makers, not just employees.

Many personally angel-invest in Indian startups alongside their day jobs, writing early checks before Indian VCs even see the deal - giving founders a direct line into how Silicon Valley actually builds and scales companies.

This isn't outside money helping India. It's Indian judgment, tested in the world's toughest startup market, choosing to bet on home again.

Sources: TiE global network data, Inc42/Tracxn venture partner tracking, NASSCOM diaspora investment reports (2025)
